output.headline: Moves $1.10M in old uncashed-check funds to the General Fund for 2019-20
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text shows two warrant counts (2,690 and 2680) and two cumulative amounts ($1,104,758.00 and $1,069,434.46), which looks like an unresolved edit.
output.summary: The board moves money from stale-dated warrants (checks never cashed) out of the funds that issued them and into the General Fund, as California Government Code Section 50053 allows. The official text lists two warrant counts (2,690 and 2680) and two totals ($1,104,758.00 and $1,069,434.46), so the final figure is not clear from the text. The figures are as of May 31, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $750,000 from the Stupski Foundation for college and career pathway advising
output.summary: The district accepts a $750,000.00 grant from the Stupski Foundation to support coordination with community organizations and advising training related to students, run through the High School Linked Learning Office. The grant period is February 1, 2020 through January 31, 2023, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $14,700 to Integral Group's Cole Administration Center contract, now up to $72,200

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $14,700.00, increasing Agreement not to exceed amount from $57,500.00 to $72,200.00

output.summary: The board amends the agreement with The Integral Group, Inc. so it pursues CHPS green-building certification instead of LEED v4 and provides building-systems and commissioning support for the data center and multipurpose building next to the administration building. The added amount is $14,700.00, raising the cap from $57,500.00 to $72,200.00.

output.headline: Hires HERTZ Environmental for $25,500 on stormwater compliance for Cole Administration Center
output.summary: The board approves an agreement with HERTZ Environmental, Inc. to prepare a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan and help the district follow state construction stormwater permit rules for the Cole Administration Center Project. Work is scheduled to start August 13, 2020 and last through December 31, 2023. The cost is $25,500.00.

output.headline: Adds $10,000 to Jensen Hughes' Fremont construction contract, now up to $86,430

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $10,000.00, which includes a $5,250.00 contingency, increasing Agreement not to exceed amount from $76,430.00 to $86,430.00

output.summary: The board amends the agreement with Jensen Hughes for extra site visits to witness fire alarm and intrusion alarm testing for Increment 2 of the Fremont New Construction Project. The added $10,000.00 includes a $5,250.00 contingency (a cushion for unexpected costs), raising the cap from $76,430.00 to $86,430.00.

output.headline: Adds $40,750 and time to Verde Design's Emerson softball field contract, now up to $307,110

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $40,750.00, which includes a $15,000.00 contingency, increasing Agreement not to exceed amount from $266,360.00 to $307,110.00

output.summary: The board amends the agreement with Verde Design for the Emerson Elementary School Soft Ball Field Project. The added $40,750.00, which includes a $15,000.00 contingency (a cushion for unexpected costs), covers reimbursable fees to the state architect's office (DSA), and raises the cap from $266,360.00 to $307,110.00. The end date moves from December 31, 2020 to June 21, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $147,000 to Byrens Kim's Madison Park expansion contract, now up to $2.84M

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $147,000.00, increasing Agreement not to exceed amount from $2,695,870.00 to $2,842,870.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title calls this an agreement for Professional Development, but the action text describes Professional Services (site design and construction administration).
output.summary: The board amends the agreement with Byrens Kim Design Works for the Madison Park Academy Expansion Project. The added $147,000.00 pays for extra site design for the Capistrano Driveway and West Parking lot, to address structural construction errors, and for extra construction administration during the longer construction period. The cap rises from $2,695,870.00 to $2,842,870.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $35,500 for DCG Strategies to manage two former district sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed of $35,500.00

output.summary: The board approves, after the fact, a consultant agreement with DCG Strategies, Inc. for asset management and real property services on the former Edward Shands Adult Education Center and former Tilden Child Development Center sites. The term started June 25, 2020, before this vote, and runs through March 15, 2021. The cost is capped at $35,500.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $7,500 for Heafey Commercial to manage two former child care sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed of $7,500.00

output.summary: The board approves, after the fact, a consultant agreement with Heafey Commercial for asset management and real property services on the former Piedmont and Webster Child Development Center sites. The term started June 25, 2020, before this vote, and runs through December 31, 2021. The cost is capped at $7,500.00.

output.headline: Expands student data the district shares with the Oakland Housing Authority
output.summary: The board amends its memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) with the Housing Authority of the City of Oakland. The district would share student directory information, summary test results (kept private) and information on students' device and internet access for students whose families get housing assistance. The funding source is listed as no fiscal impact, and all other terms stay in effect.

output.headline: Ratifies $19.44M in April 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The board approves, after the fact, the district's April 2020 payroll: 901 printed checks and 6,997 direct deposits. The total is $19,437,448.42 for April 1 through April 30, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.headline: Ratifies $19.96M in May 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The board approves, after the fact, the district's May 2020 payroll: 932 printed checks and 7,016 direct deposits. The total is $19,962,670.50 for May 1 through May 31, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.headline: Approves $16.18M in June 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The board approves the district's June 2020 payroll: 688 printed checks and 7,034 direct deposits. The total is $16,181,082.61 for June 1 through June 30, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.headline: Approves $25.40M in vendor bill payments for April 2020
output.summary: The board approves the district's accounts payable warrants (checks paying bills to vendors) for April 2020: 802 printed checks. The total is $25,400,834.92 for April 1 through April 30, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.headline: Approves $29.58M in vendor bill payments for May 2020
output.summary: The board approves the district's accounts payable warrants (checks paying bills to vendors) for May 2020: 698 printed checks. The total is $29,578,441.90 for May 1 through May 31, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.summary: The board approves the district's accounts payable warrants (checks paying bills to vendors) for June 2020: 1,153 printed checks. The total is $39,769,105.02 for June 1 through June 30, 2020. Details are in an attached exhibit.

output.headline: Lets the district borrow between its own funds for cash flow in 2020-21
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution allowing the district to temporarily borrow between eligible district funds, as needed, for cash-flow purposes during fiscal year 2020-21. The borrowed money must be repaid, under Education Code Section 42603. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Approves Oakland Adult and Career Education course offerings for 2020-21
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving the course offerings of the Oakland Adult and Career Education program for the 2020-2021 school year. The funding source is listed as no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Accepts $24,860.55 from Intel via Oakland Public Education Fund for McClymonds counselor
output.summary: The district accepts a $24,860.55 grant from the Intel Corporation, passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund, to fully fund the Remote Learning and College Counselor position at McClymonds High School for the 2020-2021 school year. It is handled by the High School Linked Learning Office.

output.headline: Adopts pay schedules for substitute teachers in the Oakland Education Association contract
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution setting district salary schedules for certificated (credentialed) substitute positions covered by the Oakland Education Association (OEA). It lists a series of percentage raises from July 2007 through July 2017, plus daily-rate rules for substitutes and retired district teachers effective January 2019 and January 2020. No dollar amounts are stated.

output.headline: Approves agreement to resolve a federal disability-discrimination civil rights matter
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving an agreement to resolve U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights matter 09-19-1027, which involved alleged discrimination based on disability. The official text states no dollar amount and does not describe the terms.

output.headline: Accepts $70,000 from Intel via Oakland Public Education Fund for Oakland Tech's Computer Academy
output.summary: The district accepts a $70,000.00 grant from the Intel Corporation, passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund, to support the Computer Academy Director's salary at Oakland Technical High School. The grant period is August 12, 2019 through July 31, 2020, which ended before this vote.

output.headline: Authorizes up to $23M for nonpublic school and agency services for special education in 2020-21

money.evidence: in a cumulative amount not to exceed $23,000,000.00

output.summary: The board adopts a resolution approving new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies that serve students in the special education program. The total for fiscal year 2020-2021 may not exceed $23,000,000.00.

output.headline: Pays PLS Surveys $10,200 for a boundary survey of the former John Swett school site
output.summary: The board approves an agreement with PLS Surveys, Inc. to produce a boundary survey and a parcel map for subdividing the former John Swett Elementary School site (the Tilden Project). The contract runs from August 27, 2020 to March 31, 2021 and costs $10,200.00.

output.headline: Accepts $1.42M from a community college grant for career-technical pathways
output.summary: The district accepts a $1,416,149.00 grant through the Bay Area Community College Consortium, with Cabrillo Community College District as the agreement partner, to support its K12 Strong Workforce Program of career-technical education pathways. It is run through the High School Linked Learning Office from July 1, 2020 through December 31, 2022.

output.headline: Adopts personnel report No. 2021-0001 from the Talent/Human Resources Department
output.summary: The board adopts the Talent/Human Resources Department's personnel report No. 2021-0001. The official text does not list the specific hires, changes or costs.

output.headline: Allows on-site student internships and career programs in 2020-21 within shelter-in-place rules
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution authorizing on-site internships and career pathway programs during the 2020-21 school year, consistent with COVID-19 shelter-in-place orders. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies Kidango lease of Castlemont High buildings for $18,000 plus $18,000 annual rent

money.evidence: for a one-time payment of $18,000.00 and $18,000.00 annual rent

output.summary: The board approves, after the fact, a lease letting Kidango, Inc. use Buildings H and I at Castlemont High School for an early childhood education and family support program for low-income children. Kidango pays a one-time $18,000.00 plus $18,000.00 annual rent. The term began July 8, 2020, before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2021.
